input.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
input.rationale: The only governing-law provision (§ 11, p0043) selects Arizona law and specifies no venue. Arizona is outside the accepted list (New York preferred; Delaware, California or England and Wales at fallback), so the clause fails the fallback on a material term. The redline changes only the jurisdiction words and adds exclusive New York County venue, leaving the severability language intact. The arbitration clause (p0056) is mandatory but administered under U.S. rules with confirmation in U.S. courts — it is not a foreign-seated arbitration and therefore not walk-away territory, so we preserve it and note only that the venue language is expressed for proceedings not resolved by arbitration.

proposal.summary: Change governing law from Arizona to New York and add exclusive New York County venue.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We moved governing law and venue to our accepted New York position; Arizona is outside our approved list (New York preferred; Delaware, California or England and Wales as fallbacks). Venue is stated for any proceeding not resolved by arbitration so the rest of the clause is unchanged.

ops.oldText: the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof, and each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York for any proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement that is not resolved by arbitration.
